source.context: Graduation capture for SN-0797: machine-readable encoding of Zeta's w141 T3 Smart Note for learn-clock lesson LC-20261014-004 (hidden_files/w141/zeta-T3-smart-note-LC-20261014-004.md, sha256 cd839b41…09cecd). The T3 note was authored by Naya Zeta (Intelligent Blocks), wave 141, lane 3; this capture only encodes it for the projection workflow. No new intelligence is asserted. Page + capture + registry entry land together in one PR so no drift class grows.

intelligence.essence: After a PR-body PATCH, verify from the PATCH response itself — never spend a second GET re-reading what the server just returned.
intelligence.human_view: When you edit a pull-request description, the server sends back the updated text in its reply. Reading it back again with a separate request is asking someone to repeat what they just said while you are holding the written answer. Check the reply you already have.
intelligence.simple_view: If your friend hands you the new drawing, you do not ask for it again — you look at the one in your hands.
intelligence.grandma_view: When the office sends back your corrected letter with the changes in it, you check that copy. You do not pay for a second copy just to check the first one.
intelligence.naya_view: Every PATCH-then-GET pair on the same body is a wasted API call against a 10-call-per-mission governor. One wasted call is small; at wave scale — every body edit, every wave — it is the difference between a wave that fits its budget and one that burns calls discovering nothing. The governor is only real if PATCH-then-GET pairs get counted as waste.
intelligence.ai_view: Learn-clock lesson LC-20261014-004 (Smart Note SN-0797, T3 DISTILLED): after PATCHing a PR body, verify from the PATCH response itself — never spend a second GET re-reading what the server just returned. Provenance: PR #2551 evidence-section re-pin, 2 calls instead of 4. Enforcement: sign-out/API-governor check counts unjustified PATCH-then-GET as a wasted call; T6 probe gate rewrites the lesson if treatment workers still re-GET. Exception: if the PATCH response lacks the body, one GET is allowed and must be named in the sign-out. T4–T6 un-emitted; T3 emit belongs to the dispatcher.

machine_view.trigger: PATCH to a PR body (e.g. evidence-section re-pin)
machine_view.rule: Assert the new body from the PATCH response object (e.g. contains_new=True, contains_old=False). Do NOT issue a GET for the same body in the same mission.
machine_view.exception: If the PATCH response does not contain the updated body, a GET is allowed — and the sign-out must name that exception.

machine_view.scope: PR-body PATCHes where the PATCH response returns the updated body. Not a general ban on GETs.

machine_view.title: PATCH response is the verify

intelligence.learning_lesson: The original event proved the saving (2 calls instead of 4) but did NOT itself teach anyone — it was the first application, before any distill or inject. A lesson only starts teaching when a *second* worker skips the re-GET *because of* it. That is the P-015 bar: name the decision that changed, or nothing was learned. The decision that must change: **skip the re-GET after a PATCH.**
intelligence.applicability:
1. After PATCHing a PR body, assert from the PATCH response object (contains_new / contains_old, or the equivalent fields).
2. Do NOT issue a GET for the same body in the same mission.
3. If the PATCH response lacks the body, a GET is allowed — name the exception in the sign-out ("PATCH response lacked the body, so one GET was justified").
4. In the lane-feed sign-out, state the call count and the skipped re-GET explicitly (e.g. "Verified from the PATCH response per LC-20261014-004; skipped the re-GET; 2 calls instead of 4") — that sentence is the T5 evidence the dispatcher watches for.
intelligence.enforcement:
- **E1 — Sign-out / API-governor check (who, when):** when the dispatcher folds a sign-out, any transcript showing a GET of a PR body immediately after a PATCH to the same body must carry the exception justification. An unjustified PATCH-then-GET counts as a **wasted call** in the wave's API-spend log. This uses existing motion (fold-in reads sign-outs) — no new tooling, no new gate.
- **E2 — T6 probe gate (what breaks if the lesson is ignored):** the lesson passes T6 only if a cold-successor probe shows treatment (brief carries the one-sentence principle) verifying from the PATCH response while control re-GETs. If treatment workers still re-GET, the lesson **FAILS T6 and is rewritten, not promoted**. The probe is the gate that breaks the lesson if it does not change behavior.
- **E3 — Scope guard:** the rule does not apply where the PATCH response omits the body. The exception must be named in the sign-out, never assumed silently — an unnamed exception is the same as ignoring the rule.
intelligence.uncertainty:
- It does NOT claim the lesson is VERIFIED — T3 is filed; T4/T5/T6 have no evidence yet, and T4–T6 are deliberately NOT emitted here.
- It does NOT claim the T3 emit has happened — the dispatcher emits T3 from the w141 receipt. This file is the evidence, not the emit.
- It does NOT claim the re-GET is never justified — a PATCH response without the body is the named exception.
- It does NOT claim Supabase holds no prior note on this lesson — Supabase was not queried (read-only law + API budget). If one exists un-emitted, the fix is to emit T3 with this evidence.
- It does NOT claim the T2 timestamp discrepancy (audit 04:47:00Z vs store 04:56:26Z) is resolved — it is flagged for the dispatcher/owner.
- It does NOT claim the probe will pass — the probe has not been run.
intelligence.successor_effect: A cold successor reading this note should: (1) after PATCHing a PR body, assert from the PATCH response object (contains_new / contains_old); (2) NOT issue a GET for the same body in the same mission; (3) if the PATCH response lacks the body, one GET is allowed — and the sign-out must name that exception; (4) state the call count and the skipped re-GET explicitly in the lane-feed sign-out.
